cards.title: Shard the Playwright e2e gate across three runners, required check name held stable

evidence.ref: #774 MERGED 2026-08-04 (5fc88a2). MEASURED, not estimated, on run 30942125889 - the first run where all three shards completed on one commit with the isolation defect fixed: shard 1 6m43s, shard 2 6m58s, shard 3 7m10s, aggregate gate 3s. Wall clock ~7m13s, and the number to quote is the SLOWEST shard, never the average. Against the same day's unsharded runs on real code changes (12m30s, 13m00s, 13m22s, 13m57s, 14m08s) that is roughly a 45% cut. The split is now even - 27s between fastest and slowest - where before the fix it ran 6m27s to 13m22s because shard 3 was spending 6.3 minutes on doomed retries, which is exactly why no figure was quoted earlier. Required check name held: 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB)' reported and passed as the aggregate, and branch protection needed NO change - the hard constraint on the whole design.

cards.notes:
Not a Wave 13 loop. Infrastructure that pays back across every PR of the wave, dispatched by the owner before LOOP 1.

THE CONSTRAINT: branch protection pins three contexts by exact string, and a check context IS a job name. Sharding the existing job in place would have renamed its checks to 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB) (1)' and friends; the required context would never report again and every PR would hang forever on a check that no longer exists. So the work moved to a job named 'E2E shard' and a new aggregate job inherits the exact old name, runs no tests, and fails unless all three shards succeeded. NO REPOSITORY SETTINGS CHANGE IS NEEDED - which was the stated fallback condition.

Workflow file and matrix only: zero test-file edits, zero playwright.config.ts edits, retries untouched (no --retries flag on pull_request, so the config's CI ? 2 : 0 still governs).

VERIFIED FROM SOURCE, NOT ASSUMED: setup runs in every shard. Pinned Playwright 1.60.0, runner/index.js:2443-2465 - the shard filter iterates rootSuite.suites, which holds top-level projects only, and dependency projects are prepended afterwards from the UNFILTERED suite. That is also why the invocation now passes --project=chromium alone: naming setup explicitly promotes it to top-level and puts its tests INTO the shard filter, the one arrangement where a shard could receive no setup tests.

THE RED PATH IS PROVEN, and not by a contrived test. A deliberate forced-failure run was planned; it turned out to be unnecessary because attempt 1 produced the exact scenario that needed proving: shard 3 genuinely failed while shards 1 and 2 passed, and the required check 'Playwright E2E (seeded DB)' went RED in 4 seconds. That is the partial-failure case - one leg red, two green - which is the one that matters and the one a designed-to-work argument could not have settled. `if: always()` plus a strict 'success' comparison behaved exactly as intended. Skipped is deliberately NOT accepted as success; this repo has already been bitten by a green that was really a skip.



--- CORRECTION AND DIAGNOSIS, 2026-08-04. THE EARLIER CHECKPOINT WAS WRONG. ---
Board checkpoint 01 (#776, merged) recorded that the cross-file-dependency hypothesis was CHECKED AND REFUTED. That was WRONG, and it was wrong because the check was too narrow: it asked who else REFERENCES the fixture constant AI_REVIEW_DRAFT, when the question that mattered was who else MUTATES the shared review queue. Correcting it here rather than leaving a merged board claim standing.

THE REAL CAUSE, proven rather than hypothesised. e2e/clinical.spec.ts:169-188 HARD-DELETES AI_DELETE_DRAFT, which fixtures.ts defines as a SECOND draft belonging to the SAME patient, Joao Pereira. e2e/revisao-consulta.spec.ts:36-39 finds its queue row by getByRole("row").filter({hasText: patientName}).first().
Unsharded, clinical.spec.ts runs BEFORE revisao-consulta.spec.ts (file order, c before r), so by the time revisao-consulta reads the queue there is exactly ONE Joao Pereira row and .first() is unambiguous.
Sharded, the local listing puts clinical.spec.ts in SHARD 1 and revisao-consulta.spec.ts in SHARD 3. AI_DELETE_DRAFT is therefore never deleted in shard 3, two Joao Pereira rows sit in the queue, and .first() selects the wrong one - whose Assumir never becomes clickable. Hence a 120s locator.click timeout, three times, 6.3 of the 10.4 minutes, which is also why shard 3 was the long pole.

THIS IS A LATENT TEST-ISOLATION DEFECT THAT SHARDING EXPOSED, NOT ONE IT CREATED. revisao-consulta.spec.ts has always depended on another spec file having run first. Any change to file order would trigger it.

PARKED per the owner ceiling of one working session. The enabling fix is one line in a TEST file - scope the row by data-record-id, exactly as clinical.spec.ts:173 already does, instead of hasText + .first() - and this PR was dispatched with zero test-file edits, so it does not belong here.

UNBLOCK CONDITION, exact: authorise the one-line test-isolation fix to e2e/revisao-consulta.spec.ts as its own PR. Once that is on main, #774 needs no change of its own - re-run its checks and all three shards should go green.
RECOMMENDED DEFAULT: authorise it. The defect is real independently of sharding and the fix makes the test say what it means.

WHAT IS ALREADY PROVEN AND SURVIVES THE PARK: the required-check name held stable (three new E2E shard (N) contexts appeared, Playwright E2E (seeded DB) kept reporting, branch protection untouched); setup ran in all three shards; and the RED PATH works - one red shard against two green produced a RED required check in 4 seconds.
WHAT IS NOT YET PROVEN: the wall-clock win. Shards 1 and 2 came in at 7m27s and 6m27s against the 13m21s baseline, but shard 3 spent 6.3 minutes on three doomed retries, so no honest speed figure exists until the test is fixed. The number to quote is the SLOWEST shard, never the average.

--- SHIPPED 2026-08-04, and the park was the right call ---
Parking it rather than merging on a red run is what produced the correct diagnosis. Merging it green-by-retry would have shipped the shard split on top of a live test-isolation defect and left the next person to find it.

The red path was proven twice over: once by accident on attempt 1 (one red shard against two green produced a RED required check in 4 seconds), and the planned deliberate forced-failure run was never needed.

cards.title: Portal deployment failure: every apps/api call from the portal is failing

evidence.ref: CLOSED 2026-08-05 on the DEPLOYED portal per WF-03. Ivan screenshots of osteojp-portal.vercel.app/portal/dashboard: "Ola, ZZ" with the greeting populated and the appointments card rendering, and /portal/appointments rendering "Nao tem consultas marcadas" - the LOADED-AND-EMPTY state, not the PL-34 error state. That distinction is the proof: before PL-34 both a real empty list and a failed fetch rendered identically.

cards.notes:
ROOT CAUSE, TWO LAYERS, BOTH PROVEN AND BOTH FIXED.

LAYER 1 - ZERO PATIENT LINKAGE. All 21 prod patients had auth_user_id NULL. The access-token hook (public.custom_access_token_hook, 0010_patient_identity_layer.sql:204-221) resolves a patient by p.auth_user_id = v_user_id; on a miss it stamps NO claims and still returns the event, so a perfectly signed token is issued carrying nothing. parsePatientPrincipal (packages/auth/patient.ts:50-56) then rejects it and every patient route 401s. No error, no log, nothing observable - which is why it survived.

LAYER 2 - STAFF IDENTITY PREEMPTION. Ivan was testing as owner staff accounts (info@a-and-i-automation.com, then ivanbong333@gmail.com, the latter proven staff role_slug=owner by the 0b check BEFORE any write). The hook checks the staff branch FIRST; a staff identity can never receive patient claims. Correct design, wrong test identity. The portal shell admits any valid session and role enforcement happens at the api, which is why login appeared to succeed while every data call 401ed.

THE FIX: a dedicated non-staff identity linked to a dedicated ZZ TESTE patient row. No real patient record was touched - linking a real patient to Ivan's login would have handed him another person's clinical data, which is the boundary this entire wave exists to defend.

BUILD HALF, closed earlier the same incident: the deployed osteojp-api was serving a stale build - /api/v1/patient/profile 404ed while /api/health answered. A no-cache rebuild of the SAME commit (1131f2d) flipped it to a correct 401. Cause confirmed, no code change.

FALSE TRAILS KILLED ALONG THE WAY, recorded so they are not re-walked: root-directory config (verified correct), deployment protection (api root page renders openly), split-brain Supabase projects (anon key identical across all three Vercel projects), stale build (production current at 1131f2d), path mismatch (both route files exist at the composed paths), middleware 404 (updateSession only ever returns NextResponse.next), and the two health-URL 404s which were CHAT GUESSES at paths that never existed - the real path is /api/health.

THE CHECK THAT PAID FOR ITSELF: step 0b, the staff-exclusion predicate, ran BEFORE any write and caught ivanbong333@gmail.com as owner staff. Without it the fix would have been applied to an identity that could never work, and the failure would have looked identical.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE WAVE, carded against LOOP 3: no patient portal login can ever have worked against prod, because provisionPatientAuthUser (activation.ts:65-95) is the ONLY code that ever wrote auth_user_id and it is registered approved:false and slated for deletion. LOOP 3 must SUPPLY the linkage mechanism, not merely replace activation.

cards.title: apps/web DB-gated harness, so LOOP 1's remaining DoD lines can be proven

evidence.ref: #791. THE THREE PIECES:
1. A test-file CONVENTION for apps/web tests needing a live database - they must SKIP cleanly when DATABASE_URL is unset, or ci.yml (which has no database) goes red. packages/db/tests/rls-harness.ts already models this with `const live = Boolean(url)` and `live ? describe : describe.skip`.

Plus the partial line - that a consumed token's response is byte-identical to a forged token's.

Three pieces landed: the suite (gates on DATABASE_URL, so ci.yml skips it cleanly), the db-tests.yml step running it against the same Supabase stack, and the skip-guard extension that makes the first two mean anything - assert-rls-executed.mjs now merges SEVERAL vitest JSON reports and hard-requires redeem.db.test.ts. cards.title: Owner ruling R4: patient linkage is phone-match at OTP claim time, and it REFUSES on anything but exactly one match
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R4, answering Q4):

"R4 - linkage mechanism (Q4): phone-match at OTP claim time, per Decision D. If EXACTLY ONE live patient row (deleted_at null, merged_into_id null, auth_user_id null) carries the proven phone, link it. Zero matches, multiple matches, or any candidate already linked: REFUSE with a clear pt-PT message directing the patient to the clinic. Card the staff-assisted activation path as post-launch. Mis-linking a medical record is the failure class the refusal exists to prevent."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. Decision D (WAVE-13.md section 1.4) makes patient login a 6-digit SMS OTP, phone only. It does not say how a proven phone number becomes a link to a patient row. Without that, LOOP 3 cannot build the claim step.

THE PREDICATE IS EXACT, and every clause of it is load-bearing. A candidate row must have deleted_at null (not soft-deleted), merged_into_id null (not the losing side of a patient merge), and auth_user_id null (not already claimed by someone). EXACTLY ONE such row must carry the proven phone. Any other count refuses. So does any candidate that is already linked - a phone reaching an already-claimed row is either a shared number or a re-registration, and neither is safe to resolve automatically.

IT IS DELIBERATELY FAIL-CLOSED AND WILL REFUSE REAL PATIENTS. Shared household numbers, a clinic row holding the wrong phone, a patient with two rows: all refuse. That is the trade the owner made explicitly, and the reason is on the ruling - mis-linking a medical record hands one patient another patient's clinical history. A refused login is an inconvenience and a phone call. A mis-link is a data breach with two named patients in it.

REQUIRED SHAPE OF THE BUILD: the refusal copy is pt-PT, in packages/i18n, and directs the patient to contact the clinic. It must NOT tell the patient which predicate failed - 'no row found' versus 'several rows found' versus 'already claimed' are three different disclosures about who else exists in the database, so the refusal is generic, exactly as the token rejection is generic under counsel's section 3. Refusal-style tests per the Decision B precedent: zero-match refuses, multi-match refuses, already-linked refuses, and the single live match links.

FOLLOW-ON CARDED: LE-staff-assisted-activation, post-launch, for the patients this legitimately locks out.

CONSUMED BY: W13-03 (LOOP 3).

cards.title: Owner ruling R5: delete sendPatientActivation - it grants a session by design and has no caller
cards.notes:
RULING, VERBATIM, OWNER 2026-08-05 (dispatch R5, answering Q5):

"R5 - sendPatientActivation (Q5): delete it. It grants a session by design, violating Decision D, and has no caller. Include a refusal-style test where applicable, per the Decision B precedent."

WHAT IT RESOLVES. WAVE-13.md LOOP 3 step 7 makes this function's fate a decision to be taken inside the loop, and section 6 halts the loop if it turns out to have a live caller. The board has carried it as a CANDIDATE FOR OUTRIGHT DELETION since seeding. It is now decided: delete.

RE-DERIVED FROM MAIN before recording, per standing rule 1.6. A full caller search across the repo (git grep over *.ts, *.tsx, *.md) returns: the definition at apps/api/lib/auth/activation.ts:167; its own test file apps/api/lib/auth/activation.test.ts (8 references, all inside that suite); a comment at apps/api/lib/notify/registry.ts:8 that already records it as DEAD CODE with no caller; and three documentation mentions. NO PRODUCTION CALL SITE EXISTS. The halt condition in LOOP 3 section 6 is therefore not triggered.

WHY DELETION RATHER THAN LEAVING IT DORMANT. It mints a Supabase RECOVERY link and delivers it by SMS. A recovery link is a session grant. Decision D says no password, no magic link, no session minted from any other artefact. Dead code that grants a session is one route handler away from being live code that grants a session, and it is registered approved:false today only because the notification registry happens to gate it. Deleting it removes the capability rather than the permission.

SIDE EFFECT THAT CLOSES A TRACKED RESIDUAL: fallback 6 in the loud-at-boot inventory (apps/api/lib/auth/activation.ts:117, PATIENT_ACTIVATION_REDIRECT_URL silently omitted) was deliberately LEFT because the code was dead. Deleting the function retires that residual instead of fixing it. Reflect that on LE-env-sweep-scope when the deletion merges, and check whether PATIENT_ACTIVATION_CHANNEL and PATIENT_ACTIVATION_REDIRECT_URL become unreferenced.

TEST OBLIGATION. 'Refusal-style test where applicable' per the Decision B precedent: after deletion there is no function left to test, so the enforceable artefact is a test asserting that NO code path mints a Supabase recovery link or any other session for a patient. That is the property Decision D actually protects, and it survives the function it was written about.

CONSUMED BY: W13-03 (LOOP 3).
